medium.en: Handscroll, ink and colour on silk

note.zh:
南唐后主李煜怀疑大臣韩熙载夜夜宴饮、心怀异志，派宫廷画师顾闳中前往赴宴，凭记忆画下所见——这是一份用绘画完成的密报。

全卷五段：听乐、观舞、暂歇、清吹、送别，用屏风分隔，如同电影分镜。最耐人寻味的是韩熙载本人：所有人都在欢闹，只有他神情疏离、目光落空。他知道自己被看着，于是把纵情享乐演成了一种自保。
note.en:
Li Yu, last ruler of the Southern Tang, suspected his minister Han Xizai of nightly revels and disloyalty, and sent the court painter Gu Hongzhong to attend a banquet and record from memory what he saw. The scroll is an intelligence report executed in paint.

Five scenes — listening to the pipa, watching the dance, resting, the flutes, farewell — separated by folding screens like film cuts. The strangest thing is Han Xizai himself: everyone else is enjoying the party and his gaze is empty and elsewhere. He knew he was being watched, and performed his dissipation as self-protection.

look.zh: 所有人都在欢闹，只有韩熙载目光落空——他知道自己被监视。
look.en: Everyone is enjoying the party except Han Xizai. He knows he is being watched.

src.file: File:Gu Hongzhong's Night Revels 1 edit (cropped).jpg

medium.en: Hanging scroll, ink and colour on silk

note.zh:
中国绘画史上最有分量的一张画。巨大的山壁占据画面上三分之二，几乎压下来；山脚的树林里，一队驮着货物的旅人和一头驴正在走过，小到几乎看不见。人与山的比例，就是宋人的宇宙观。

范宽用密集短促的「雨点皴」堆出岩体的粗粝。1958年，研究者在右下角树丛的暗处发现了「范宽」二字签名——藏了九百多年。据说他常年独居终南山中，师法自然而不师古人。
note.en:
The weightiest painting in Chinese art. A single cliff fills the upper two-thirds and seems about to come down; at its foot a train of pack animals and drivers moves through the trees, almost too small to find. The ratio of people to mountain is the Song view of the cosmos.

Fan Kuan built the rock from dense short "raindrop" strokes. In 1958 scholars found his signature hidden in the dark foliage at the lower right, concealed for over nine hundred years. He is said to have lived for years alone in the Zhongnan mountains, taking nature rather than earlier masters as his teacher.

look.zh: 右下角树丛暗处藏着「范宽」二字，1958年才被发现。
look.en: His signature hides in the dark foliage at lower right. It was found only in 1958.

src.file: File:Fan Kuan - Travelers Among Mountains and Streams - Google Art Project.jpg

medium.en: Hanging scroll, ink and colour on silk

note.zh:
北宋山水的巅峰之一，画的是冬末春初、冰雪初融、雾气升起的一刻。郭熙在《林泉高致》里提出「三远」：高远（自下仰望）、深远（自前窥后）、平远（自近眺远），这幅画在一张绢上同时用了三种。

他的山石用「卷云皴」，石块像云一样翻卷、彼此推挤，整座山因此在呼吸。树是「蟹爪枝」，枯枝向下勾曲。画中有渔人、樵夫、旅人、僧侣——山永远比人大得多，但人从不缺席。
note.en:
One of the summits of Northern Song landscape, showing the moment at winter's end when ice melts and vapour begins to rise. In his treatise Guo Xi set out the "three distances" — looking up from below, looking through from front to back, looking out across the level — and used all three on this single sheet of silk.

His rocks are built with the "rolling cloud" texture stroke, so the stone curls and jostles and the whole mountain breathes. The trees are "crab-claw" branches, hooking downward. Fishermen, woodcutters, travellers and monks appear throughout: the mountain always dwarfs them, and they are never absent.

look.zh: 山石用「卷云皴」画成——整座山像在呼吸。
look.en: The rocks use the rolling-cloud stroke. The whole mountain seems to breathe.

src.file: File:Guo Xi - Early Spring (large).jpg

title.en: A Thousand Li of Rivers and Mountains

medium.en: Handscroll, ink and colour on silk

note.zh:
王希孟画这卷时十八岁，由宋徽宗亲自指点，此后不久去世，再无其他作品传世。近十二米的绢上，青绿山水连绵不断，其中的石青、石绿来自研磨的孔雀石与蓝铜矿，近千年后仍未褪色。

画中有村落、渔舟、水磨、长桥、书院——山水不是空景，而是可居可游的世界。这卷因颜料层厚重、每次展卷都会剥落，故宫极少展出，二〇一七年一次公开展览排队超过六小时。
note.en:
Wang Ximeng was eighteen when he painted this under the personal instruction of Emperor Huizong; he died soon afterward and nothing else by him survives. Across nearly twelve metres of silk the blue-green mountains run unbroken, their azurite and malachite pigments ground from stone and still unfaded after nine centuries.

There are villages, fishing boats, water mills, long bridges and academies: this landscape is not empty scenery but a world to live and travel in. The pigment layer flakes each time the scroll is opened, so the Palace Museum shows it very rarely — a 2017 display drew queues of more than six hours.

look.zh: 石青石绿由孔雀石与蓝铜矿研磨而成，近千年不褪。
look.en: The blues and greens are ground azurite and malachite. Nine centuries, unfaded.

src.file: File:Wang Ximeng. A Thousand Li of Rivers and Mountains. (Complete, 51,3x1191,5 cm). 1113. Palace museum, Beijing.jpg

title.en: Along the River During the Qingming Festival (detail)

medium.en: Handscroll, ink and colour on silk

note.zh:
北宋汴京（今开封）的城市全景，全卷五米多长，可辨认人物八百余、牲畜六十余、船二十余、房屋楼宇三十余栋。手卷不是用来挂的，而是在案上一段段展开、一段段收起，观看本身就是一次行走。

最著名的一段是虹桥：一艘大船正要撞上桥，桅杆来不及放倒，桥上桥下几十个人在同时喊叫。整幅长卷没有一处高潮，也没有主角——它是中国绘画里最接近纪录片的一件作品。
note.en:
A panorama of Bianjing (modern Kaifeng), capital of the Northern Song: over five metres long, with more than eight hundred identifiable figures, sixty animals, twenty boats and thirty buildings. A handscroll is not hung; it is opened arm's length at a time on a table, so viewing it is itself a walk.

The famous passage is the Rainbow Bridge, where a large boat is about to strike it, the mast not lowered in time, and dozens of people above and below are shouting at once. Nothing in the scroll is a climax and no one is the protagonist. It is the closest thing in Chinese painting to documentary.

look.zh: 手卷要一段段展开看——虹桥撞船那段是全卷唯一的「事故」。
look.en: Open it a span at a time. The boat about to hit the Rainbow Bridge is the only accident in it.

src.file: File:Along the River During the Qingming Festival (detail of original).jpg

note.zh:
黄公望七十九岁开始画，断断续续三四年才完成，画的是富春江两岸。他不再追求宋人的雄伟压迫，而用干笔皴擦，让山水显得松、淡、可亲——文人画从这里定下基调。

此卷命运离奇：明末收藏家吴洪裕临终前要焚画殉葬，被侄子从火中抢出，已烧成两段。前段《剩山图》现藏浙江省博物馆，后段《无用师卷》藏台北故宫。2011年两段曾在台北合璧展出，隔了三百六十年。
note.en:
Huang Gongwang began at seventy-nine and worked on and off for three or four years, painting both banks of the Fuchun River. He gave up the crushing grandeur of the Song for dry, scrubbed brushwork — loose, pale, companionable — and set the key for literati painting thereafter.

Its history is extraordinary. The late-Ming collector Wu Hongyu ordered it burned for his own funeral; his nephew pulled it from the fire in two pieces. The shorter fragment is in the Zhejiang Provincial Museum and the longer in Taipei. The two halves were reunited for an exhibition in 2011, after 360 years apart.

look.zh: 这卷曾被主人下令焚烧殉葬，从火里抢出时已断成两截。
look.en: Its owner ordered it burned with him. It was pulled from the fire in two pieces.

src.file: File:Huang Gongwang. Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains. detail. National Palace Museum, Taipei.jpg

note.zh:
弗拉·安杰利科是多明我会修士，作画前必先祷告，据说画基督受难时会流泪。这幅画把两件事并置：右侧凉廊里天使向马利亚宣告，左侧花园中亚当夏娃正被逐出伊甸——原罪与救赎，用一根柱子隔开。

凉廊的透视是刚从布鲁内莱斯基那里学来的新技术，而金色的光线、繁密的花草仍属于中世纪。这幅画正站在两个时代的门槛上。天使翅膀上的彩色是用真金打底后罩染而成。
note.en:
Fra Angelico was a Dominican friar who prayed before painting and is said to have wept while painting the Crucifixion. Two events sit side by side here: in the loggia at the right the angel addresses Mary; in the garden at the left Adam and Eve are being expelled. The Fall and the Redemption, separated by one column.

The loggia's perspective is the new technique just learned from Brunelleschi, while the gold light and the crowded flowers still belong to the Middle Ages. The picture stands on the threshold between two eras. The angel's wing colours are glazed over a ground of real gold.

look.zh: 一根柱子隔开了两件事：左边是失乐园，右边是救赎的开始。
look.en: One column separates the Fall on the left from the Redemption beginning on the right.

src.file: File:Fra Angelico 095.jpg

title.zh: 根特祭坛画（神秘羔羊之爱）

note.zh:
十二块面板、上下两层，被认为是欧洲第一件充分发挥油画媒介的巨作。中央下方，神秘的羔羊立于祭坛，血流入圣杯，四方人群从画面各处朝它汇聚。

它也是世界上失窃次数最多的艺术品：至少被偷或被劫十三次，拿破仑拿走过，纳粹藏进奥地利盐矿。1934年被盗的《公正的法官》一板至今下落不明，现在挂着的是复制品。2010年代的修复揭开了后世覆盖的颜料，露出羔羊那双异常拟人的正面眼睛。
note.en:
Twelve panels in two tiers, widely regarded as the first monumental work to exploit oil paint fully. In the lower centre the Mystic Lamb stands on an altar, its blood running into a chalice as crowds converge from every corner of the picture.

It is also the most stolen artwork in history — taken or looted at least thirteen times, carried off by Napoleon, hidden by the Nazis in an Austrian salt mine. The Just Judges panel, stolen in 1934, has never been found; a copy hangs in its place. Restoration in the 2010s stripped away later overpaint and uncovered the Lamb's disconcertingly human, forward-facing eyes.

look.zh: 左下角那块《公正的法官》是复制品——原作1934年失窃，至今未找到。
look.en: The lower-left panel is a copy: the original was stolen in 1934 and never recovered.

src.file: File:Lamgods open.jpg

note.zh:
油画技术早期最惊人的一次演示。凡·艾克用极薄的油性罩染叠出黄铜吊灯的反光、狗毛的每一根卷曲、窗外的樱桃树——尺寸只有A2纸大小。

后墙的凸面镜里映出房间全景，还有两个站在门口的人影；镜子上方用花体拉丁文写着「扬·凡·艾克曾在此，1434」。这不像签名，更像证词。这幅画到底是婚礼、订婚还是纪念亡妻，学界争了一个世纪，仍无定论。
note.en:
An early and astonishing demonstration of what oil paint could do. Van Eyck built the brass chandelier's reflections, every curl of the dog's coat, and a cherry tree outside the window from glazes thinner than paper — on a panel the size of a sheet of A2.

The convex mirror on the back wall shows the whole room and two figures in the doorway, and above it, in flourished Latin: "Jan van Eyck was here, 1434." That reads less like a signature than like testimony. Whether the picture records a wedding, a betrothal or a dead wife has been argued for a century without resolution.

look.zh: 凑近后墙的凸面镜——里面有第三、第四个人。
look.en: Go close to the convex mirror: there are a third and a fourth person in the room.

src.file: File:Van Eyck - Arnolfini Portrait.jpg

note.zh:
乌切洛痴迷透视到了病态的程度——瓦萨里说他妻子半夜叫他睡觉，他答「多么甜美的透视啊」。这幅画里，地上折断的长矛全部朝向同一组消失点，倒地的士兵被画成严格的短缩透视，像一道解几何题。

结果是奇特的：战斗被冻结成了一场精密的仪式，马匹像木马，铠甲反光如金属静物。这是三联作之一，另两幅分藏乌菲齐与卢浮宫——十九世纪被拆散出售，至今未能重聚。
note.en:
Uccello's obsession with perspective was close to pathological. Vasari reports that when his wife called him to bed at night he answered, "What a sweet thing this perspective is." Here the broken lances on the ground all align to a single set of vanishing points and a fallen soldier is drawn in strict foreshortening, like a geometry exercise worked out in paint.

The effect is peculiar: the battle freezes into a precise ceremony, the horses read as carousel animals and the armour as metal still life. This is one of three panels; the others are in the Uffizi and the Louvre, split up and sold in the nineteenth century and never reunited.

look.zh: 地上折断的长矛全部指向同一组消失点。
look.en: Every broken lance on the ground aligns to the same vanishing points.

src.file: File:San Romano Battle (Paolo Uccello, London) 01.jpg

note.zh:
要从右往左读：西风神追逐宁芙克罗丽丝，她口中吐出花朵，变形为花神芙罗拉；中央维纳斯统辖这座果园，头顶是蒙眼的丘比特；左侧三美神起舞，墨丘利用手杖拨开云雾。

植物学家在画中辨认出约190种植物，其中130余种可确定物种，全部是佛罗伦萨春季实际开放的花。这幅画大概是文艺复兴最难解的图像谜题，五百年来的解释包括新柏拉图主义寓言、婚礼贺礼、美第奇家族政治宣言，没有一种被公认。
note.en:
Read it right to left: Zephyr seizes the nymph Chloris, who breathes out flowers and transforms into Flora; Venus presides over the orchard with a blindfolded Cupid overhead; the Three Graces dance at the left while Mercury parts the clouds with his staff.

Botanists have identified around 190 plants here, more than 130 to species — all of them flowering in a Florentine spring. It is probably the hardest iconographic puzzle of the Renaissance; five centuries of readings include Neoplatonic allegory, wedding gift and Medici political statement, and none has won.

look.zh: 从右往左读——克罗丽丝口中吐出的花，正在把她变成花神。
look.en: Read right to left: the flowers from Chloris's mouth are turning her into Flora.

src.file: File:Botticelli-primavera.jpg

note.zh:
文艺复兴第一批以异教神话为主题的大幅作品之一。波提切利没有追求解剖的正确——维纳斯的脖颈过长、左肩的接法在人体上不可能，但整个身体因此变成了一条流动的曲线，像贝壳边缘的延续。

他用蛋彩而非油彩，颜色因此薄而干净；发丝与衣褶的金线是真的金粉。西风神与花神从左侧吹来，右侧的时序女神递上织锦——这不是出生，而是「美」登陆人间的仪式。
note.en:
One of the first large paintings of the Renaissance to take a pagan myth as its subject. Botticelli was not after anatomical truth: Venus's neck is too long and her left shoulder joins in a way no body allows, but the result is a single continuous curve, an extension of the shell's rim.

He worked in tempera rather than oil, so the colour stays thin and clean, and the gold in the hair and drapery is real gold. Zephyr blows in from the left, an Hour offers a cloak on the right. This is less a birth than a ceremony: beauty making landfall.

look.zh: 看她的重心——她其实站不稳，全靠曲线在支撑。
look.en: Check her balance: she could not actually stand. The curve carries her instead.

src.file: File:Sandro Botticelli - La nascita di Venere - Google Art Project - edited.jpg

note.zh:
画中人是切奇莉娅·加莱拉尼，米兰公爵卢多维科·斯福尔扎十六岁的情人。她怀里那只白鼬（银鼠）是双关：希腊语中银鼠称 galé，谐她的姓；而公爵本人的绰号正是「白鼬」。

真正的革新是姿态。此前的女性肖像几乎全是静止的侧面，达·芬奇让她的身体、脖颈与目光转向三个不同方向，仿佛刚有人叫了她的名字。她的右手按在鼬身上，指节的紧张感与动物的警觉完全同步。
note.en:
The sitter is Cecilia Gallerani, sixteen-year-old mistress of Ludovico Sforza, Duke of Milan. The ermine is a double pun: the Greek for the animal, galé, echoes her surname, and the Duke's own nickname was the Ermine.

The real innovation is the pose. Female portraits had been static profiles; Leonardo turns her body, neck and gaze in three different directions, as though someone has just spoken her name. Her right hand presses into the animal's fur, and the tension in her knuckles is exactly the tension in the ermine.

look.zh: 她的身体、脖子、眼睛朝向三个方向——像刚被人叫住。
look.en: Body, neck and eyes face three different ways, as if she has just been called.

src.file: File:Lady with an Ermine - Leonardo da Vinci (adjusted levels).jpg

medium.en: Tempera and oil on dry plaster

note.zh:
达·芬奇不愿受湿壁画「必须一气呵成」的限制，改用干壁上的蛋彩与油彩，好让自己反复修改。代价是：画完二十年就开始剥落，如今我们看到的大部分是历代修复的痕迹。

他选的瞬间是基督刚说完「你们中有一人要出卖我」。十二使徒被分成四组三人，像声波一样从中心扩散出去；犹大是唯一身体后仰、脸落在暗处的人，手里攥着钱袋。所有透视线消失在基督右眼——他是这个房间的几何中心。
note.en:
Leonardo refused the discipline of true fresco, which must be finished wet and cannot be revised, and used tempera and oil on dry plaster so he could keep changing it. It began flaking within twenty years, and most of what we see now is centuries of restoration.

The moment is just after "one of you will betray me." The twelve are grouped in fours of three, the shock spreading outward like a wave. Judas alone leans back into shadow, clutching a purse. Every perspective line converges on Christ's right eye: he is the geometric centre of the room.

look.zh: 所有透视线交于基督的右眼。
look.en: Every vanishing line meets at Christ's right eye.

src.file: File:Leonardo da Vinci (1452-1519) - The Last Supper (1495-1498).jpg

note.zh:
三联画从左到右读：伊甸园里上帝把夏娃交给亚当；中幅是数百个赤裸的人在巨型果实与幻想生物之间游戏；右幅是一座黑色的地狱，乐器变成刑具，一个人被钉在竖琴上。

博斯的图像学至今没有定论——是道德警告，还是异端狂想？可以确定的是他的想象力密度：中幅每平方尺都有独立的小故事，看半小时也数不完。合上双翼时，外侧画的是灰色的创世第三日，一个玻璃球里的世界。
note.en:
Read left to right: in Eden, God presents Eve to Adam; in the centre, hundreds of naked figures play among giant fruit and invented creatures; on the right, a black hell where musical instruments have become instruments of torture and a man is crucified on a harp.

The iconography has never been settled — moral warning or heretical fantasy? What is certain is the density of invention: every square foot of the central panel holds its own small narrative. Closed, the outer wings show the third day of creation in grisaille, a world inside a glass sphere.

look.zh: 右联的「树人」有一张回望的脸——许多人认为那是博斯的自画像。
look.en: The Tree-Man in hell looks back over his shoulder. Many read that face as Bosch's self-portrait.

src.file: File:The Garden of earthly delights.jpg

note.zh:
达·芬奇用一生反复修改这块不到两平方尺的白杨木板。他把「晕涂法」推到极致——轮廓不再由线条界定，而是让颜料一层层薄如烟雾地叠上去，眼角与嘴角因此永远处在将笑未笑之间。你以为她在笑，移开视线又觉得她收了笑意，这种不稳定正是画面魔力的来源。

背景是一片没有具体地名的原始山水，左右两侧的地平线并不等高，视线在两边游移时，人物仿佛也在微微转动。这幅画在1911年被盗、两年后寻回，那场轰动才把它推上「世界最著名绘画」的位置。
note.en:
Leonardo reworked this small poplar panel for most of his later life. He pushed sfumato to its limit: no contour is drawn, only translucent glazes laid smoke-thin over one another, so the corners of the eyes and mouth are permanently suspended between expressions.

The landscape behind her belongs to no real place, and the horizon sits at different heights on either side — glance from one to the other and the figure seems to shift. The 1911 theft, and its recovery two years later, is what turned a famous painting into the most famous painting on earth.

look.zh: 盯住她的嘴角，再用余光看——笑意会自己出现又消失。
look.en: Stare at the mouth, then look away: the smile arrives only in peripheral vision.

src.file: File:Mona Lisa, by Leonardo da Vinci, from C2RMF retouched.jpg

note.zh:
西方绘画史上最著名的「不知道在画什么」。一个持杖的年轻男子，一位在哺乳的裸女，中间隔着一条河和两截断柱，天边一道闪电。五百年来的解释有几十种，无一成立。

X光检测显示，男子的位置原本画的是另一个裸女——乔尔乔内在作画中途改了主意。这幅画的重点或许不在故事，而在于它是欧洲第一批「风景不再是背景」的作品：人物成了气氛的注脚。
note.en:
The most famous "nobody knows" in Western painting. A young man with a staff, a nursing nude, a river and two broken columns between them, a lightning bolt at the horizon. Dozens of readings over five centuries; none holds.

X-rays show another female nude where the man now stands — Giorgione changed his mind mid-picture. Perhaps the subject was never the story. This is among the first European paintings in which landscape stops being background and the figures become a footnote to weather.

look.zh: X光下，男子原本是另一个裸女。
look.en: Under X-ray, the man was originally a second nude.

src.file: File:Giorgione 019.jpg

museum.zh: 梵蒂冈博物馆 签字厅

note.zh:
教皇尤利乌斯二世书房墙上的哲学寓言。所有消失线汇聚于中央两人之间：柏拉图指天（理念世界），亚里士多德手掌向下压（现世经验）——西方思想的两条路线，用一个手势讲完。

拉斐尔把当代人画进古代：柏拉图的脸是达·芬奇，前景台阶上斜倚的赫拉克利特是米开朗基罗（后期才加上去，用的是米氏刚完成的西斯廷风格），右下角戴黑帽望向观者的年轻人是拉斐尔自己。
note.en:
A philosophical allegory on the wall of Julius II's library. Every orthogonal converges between the two central figures: Plato points up to the world of forms, Aristotle presses his palm down toward experience — the two roads of Western thought settled in one pair of gestures.

Raphael put his contemporaries into antiquity. Plato has Leonardo's face; the brooding Heraclitus sprawled on the steps is Michelangelo, added late in the sculptural manner of the just-finished Sistine ceiling; and the young man in the black cap at lower right, looking out at us, is Raphael.

look.zh: 右下角戴黑帽看向你的年轻人，就是拉斐尔本人。
look.en: The young man in the black cap at lower right, meeting your eye, is Raphael.

src.file: File:"The School of Athens" by Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino.jpg

museum.zh: 梵蒂冈博物馆 西斯廷礼拜堂

note.zh:
西斯廷天顶九幅创世图之一。米开朗基罗自称是雕塑家而非画家，四年间仰头作画，脖颈落下终身的毛病。他把神性画成了肌肉与重量。

两只手指之间留着不到一指的空隙——生命尚未传递，那道缝隙才是主题。上帝身后包裹众天使的红色斗篷，其外形与人脑的矢状剖面高度吻合，1990年一位医生在《美国医学会杂志》上提出此说，至今仍是艺术史里最迷人的争论之一。
note.en:
One of nine Genesis scenes on the Sistine ceiling. Michelangelo insisted he was a sculptor, not a painter; four years of working overhead left him with lifelong neck trouble. He painted divinity as muscle and weight.

Less than a finger's width separates the two hands. Life has not yet passed across, and that gap is the subject. The red cloak enclosing God and the angels matches the sagittal section of a human brain closely enough that a physician published the claim in JAMA in 1990 — still one of art history's most enjoyable arguments.

look.zh: 两指之间从未接触——留白才是全画的主语。
look.en: The fingers never touch. The gap is the subject.

src.file: File:Michelangelo - Creation of Adam (cropped).jpg

museum.zh: 德累斯顿历代大师画廊

note.zh:
圣母抱着圣婴从云中走来，绿色帷幕刚被拉开，两侧圣人跪着让路。她赤足踩在云上，眼神却不安——拉斐尔画的是一位知道结局的母亲。

最著名的却是底部那两个托腮的小天使。它们本是构图收尾的填充，十九世纪以后被从画里剪出来，印在明信片、糖盒和无数商品上，成为西方最泛滥的图像之一。原作被萨克森选帝侯买下，二战后曾运往莫斯科，1955年归还德累斯顿。
note.en:
The Virgin walks out of cloud with the Child, a green curtain just drawn back, saints kneeling aside. She is barefoot on the cloud and her eyes are uneasy: Raphael painted a mother who knows how it ends.

What became famous, though, is the pair of bored cherubs along the bottom edge. They were compositional filler; from the nineteenth century onward they were cropped out and printed on postcards, chocolate boxes and everything else, becoming one of the most reproduced images in the West. The picture was bought by the Elector of Saxony, taken to Moscow after the Second World War, and returned to Dresden in 1955.

look.zh: 底下那两个托腮小天使，原本只是构图的补白。
look.en: The two chin-propped cherubs at the bottom began as filler.

src.file: File:RAFAEL - Madonna Sixtina (Gemäldegalerie Alter Meister, Dresden, 1513-14. Óleo sobre lienzo, 265 x 196 cm).jpg

note.zh:
阿里阿德涅被忒修斯遗弃在纳克索斯岛，正回头望向远去的船；酒神巴克斯从战车上一跃而下，几乎悬在半空。提香把「一见钟情」画成了一个物理事件——一个身体在空中，重心还没落地。

左上角八颗星组成的星座，是巴克斯即将抛上天空的阿里阿德涅王冠。那片天空用的是当时最昂贵的群青（青金石研磨），提香把整块画布的预算押在了蓝色上。
note.en:
Abandoned by Theseus on Naxos, Ariadne turns toward the receding ship; Bacchus leaps from his chariot and hangs, mid-air. Titian painted love at first sight as a physics event — a body airborne, its weight not yet landed.

The eight stars at upper left are the crown Bacchus will throw into the sky. That blue is ultramarine, ground lapis lazuli and the most expensive pigment available; Titian spent the picture's budget on the air.

look.zh: 巴克斯整个人在半空，没有一处受力点。
look.en: Bacchus is entirely airborne, with nothing bearing his weight.

src.file: File:Titian - Bacchus and Ariadne - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
两位法国使节站在一架摆满器物的柜子两侧：天球仪、日晷、地球仪、鲁特琴、算术书、路德派赞美诗集。上层是天，下层是地，是当时知识的全部清单。鲁特琴有一根弦断了——和谐已经破裂，暗指宗教改革带来的分裂。

地板上那块斜拉变形的东西，从画面右下方低角度斜看，会还原成一个清晰的骷髅。荷尔拜因把「记住你终将死去」藏成了一个需要走位才能看见的机关。
note.en:
Two French envoys flank a cabinet loaded with instruments: celestial globe, sundials, terrestrial globe, lute, an arithmetic book, a Lutheran hymnal. Heaven on the upper shelf, earth below — the complete inventory of contemporary knowledge. One lute string is broken: harmony has failed, a pointed reference to the Reformation.

The smeared shape on the floor resolves into a precise skull when viewed from the lower right at a sharp angle. Holbein hid his memento mori as a mechanism that only works if you move.

look.zh: 从画面右下角低角度斜看地板——骷髅会显形。
look.en: View the floor from the lower right at a sharp angle: a skull appears.

src.file: File:Hans Holbein the Younger - The Ambassadors - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
名义上是女神，实际上是一间十六世纪威尼斯卧室。提香把乔尔乔内那个睡在户外的裸体维纳斯搬进室内，睁开眼睛，直视观者——神话的外衣从此变得很薄。

右侧两名侍女正在箱柜里翻找衣物，脚边一只小狗蜷着睡（狗在当时是忠贞的象征，但它睡着了）。马克·吐温看过后写道，这是「世界上最下流也最美的一张画」。
note.en:
Nominally a goddess, actually a sixteenth-century Venetian bedroom. Titian took Giorgione's Venus, asleep outdoors, brought her inside and opened her eyes to meet ours — after which the mythological alibi wore very thin.

Two maids search a chest for clothes at the right, and a small dog sleeps at her feet. Dogs meant fidelity; this one is asleep. Mark Twain called it the foulest and most beautiful picture in the world.

look.zh: 脚边的小狗象征忠贞——但它睡着了。
look.en: The dog at her feet means fidelity. It is asleep.

src.file: File:Tiziano - Venere di Urbino - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
一幅画里塞进了一百多条尼德兰谚语，每一条都被字面化：有人把头往砖墙上撞，有人给魔鬼剃胡子，有人在用玫瑰喂猪，屋顶上真的铺满了馅饼（「屋顶铺馅饼」＝富足得荒唐）。

勃鲁盖尔不是在编笑话集。整座村庄的人都在做徒劳、颠倒、自欺的事，蓝色斗篷（妻子给丈夫披蓝斗篷＝出轨）在正中央。这是关于人类愚行的百科全书，也是一张需要逐格阅读的画。
note.en:
More than a hundred Dutch proverbs packed into one panel and taken literally: a man bangs his head against a brick wall, another shaves the devil, someone scatters roses before swine, and the roof really is tiled with pies (absurd abundance).

This is not a joke collection. An entire village is busy with futile, inverted, self-deceiving acts, and the blue cloak — a wife draping one over her husband, meaning she is deceiving him — sits at dead centre. An encyclopaedia of human folly, to be read square by square.

look.zh: 正中央那件蓝斗篷是全画的枢纽——它的意思是「戴绿帽」。
look.en: The blue cloak at the centre is the hinge of the picture: it means being deceived.

src.file: File:Pieter Brueghel the Elder - The Dutch Proverbs - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
卢浮宫最大的一幅画，将近七十平方米，一百三十多个人物。它挂在《蒙娜丽莎》正对面——绝大多数游客背对着它排队。

委罗内塞把圣经故事搬进了十六世纪的威尼斯：宾客穿当代华服，桌上是威尼斯玻璃器皿，前景有狗和侏儒。基督在画面正中，几乎被淹没在喧闹里；他头顶正上方，仆人在切肉——这是全画唯一的宗教暗示（献祭）。1797年拿破仑军队将它从威尼斯掠走，为便于运输，曾把画布拦腰切开。
note.en:
The largest painting in the Louvre — nearly seventy square metres and more than a hundred and thirty figures. It hangs directly opposite the Mona Lisa, and most visitors queue with their backs to it.

Veronese moved the biblical story into sixteenth-century Venice: contemporary finery, Venetian glassware on the tables, dogs and a dwarf in the foreground. Christ sits at the centre and is nearly drowned in the noise; directly above his head a servant carves meat, the picture's one religious signal — sacrifice. Napoleon's troops looted it from Venice in 1797 and cut the canvas in half to move it.

look.zh: 基督正上方，仆人正在切肉——那是全画唯一的宗教暗示。
look.en: Directly above Christ a servant carves meat: the only religious signal in the picture.

src.file: File:Les Noces de Cana - Paolo Veronese - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 142 ; MR 384.jpg

note.zh:
塔的原型是勃鲁盖尔在罗马见过的斗兽场——他把一座异教废墟改造成了人类傲慢的纪念碑。塔身有八层拱廊，砖砌与山岩交错，塔顶仍在施工，云已经在半腰处飘过。

最致命的细节是结构：塔的每一层都不是水平的，整座建筑向左倾斜，拱券的走向暴露了地基的下沉。工程还没停，失败已经写进了砖缝里。左下角，尼姆罗德王正在视察，工匠们跪伏在地。
note.en:
The model for the tower is the Colosseum, which Bruegel had seen in Rome — a pagan ruin converted into a monument to human presumption. Eight tiers of arcades wind upward, brickwork cut into living rock, the summit still under construction while cloud drifts past the middle floors.

The fatal detail is structural: no storey is level, the whole mass leans to the left, and the arcades betray a foundation already settling. Work has not stopped and the failure is written into the mortar. At the lower left King Nimrod inspects the site while masons prostrate themselves.

look.zh: 每一层都不水平——地基在下沉，塔却还在往上盖。
look.en: No storey is level. The foundation is sinking and they are still building.

src.file: File:Pieter Bruegel the Elder - The Tower of Babel (Vienna) - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
「月令组画」六幅中的十二月至一月。三个猎人带着一群疲惫的狗从左侧下坡，只猎到一只狐狸；他们低头走，脊背弯着——欧洲绘画里第一次，劳动者的疲倦成了主题。

1565年正处于「小冰期」最冷的年份之一。勃鲁盖尔用一条从左上到右下的对角线（树、狗、山坡）把视线送进远处的冰湖，湖上有人在滑冰、打冰球。塔可夫斯基在《飞向太空》里让镜头在这幅画上停留了近三分钟。
note.en:
December–January from Bruegel's cycle of the months. Three hunters come downhill from the left with a string of exhausted dogs and a single fox. They walk with their heads down and their backs bent: the first time in European painting that the fatigue of labour is the subject.

1565 fell in one of the coldest stretches of the Little Ice Age. A diagonal of trees, dogs and slope carries the eye down to a frozen lake where people skate and play at curling. Tarkovsky held the camera on this painting for nearly three minutes in Solaris.

look.zh: 猎物只有一只狐狸——这是一次失败的狩猎。
look.en: The whole catch is one fox. This hunt has failed.

src.file: File:Pieter Bruegel the Elder - Hunters in the Snow (Winter) - Google Art Project.jpg

museum.zh: 圣路易吉·德·弗朗西斯教堂

note.zh:
税吏马太与同伙在昏暗的房间里数钱，基督从右侧走进来，抬手一指。那道从右上方斜射的光跟着手势进来，把整间屋子劈成两半——卡拉瓦乔的「明暗对照」不是照明，是叙事本身。

基督的手势直接引自米开朗基罗《创造亚当》里上帝的手，只是无力地垂着。至今争论不休的是：被指的到底是哪一个？那个低头数钱、什么也没听见的年轻人，可能才是马太。
note.en:
The tax collector and his associates count money in a dim room; Christ enters from the right and raises a hand. A shaft of light comes in with the gesture and splits the room in two. Caravaggio's chiaroscuro is not lighting — it is the narration.

Christ's hand quotes God's hand from Michelangelo's Creation of Adam, but hangs limp. What is still argued is who is being called: the young man bent over the coins, who has heard nothing at all, may be the real Matthew.

look.zh: 光的方向和基督的手势完全一致——光就是那声召唤。
look.en: The light travels exactly along Christ's gesture. The light is the summons.

src.file: File:The Calling of Saint Matthew-Caravaggo (1599-1600).jpg

note.zh:
复活后的基督与两位门徒同桌，他掰饼的一刻，门徒才认出他。卡拉瓦乔选的正是「认出」发生的那一秒：左边的人抓紧椅子要站起来，右边的人双臂猛地张开——他的右手几乎伸出画面，撞向观者。

桌沿的果篮悬在边缘，随时要掉下去，是整幅画最紧张的物件。基督被画成无须的年轻人，这在当时引起过非议。卡拉瓦乔用的模特是罗马街头的普通人，圣徒穿着破了洞的衣服。
note.en:
The risen Christ at table with two disciples, recognised only when he breaks the bread. Caravaggio chose the exact second of recognition: the man on the left grips his chair to rise, the one on the right flings his arms wide — his right hand almost leaves the canvas and lands in our space.

The fruit basket teeters on the table edge, the most anxious object in the picture. Christ is beardless and young, which offended contemporaries. Caravaggio's models were people off the Roman streets, and his saints wear clothes with holes in them.

look.zh: 桌沿的果篮正要掉下去——它是整幅画的紧张所在。
look.en: The fruit basket is about to fall. That is where the tension lives.

src.file: File:1602-3 Caravaggio,Supper at Emmaus National Gallery, London.jpg

artist.zh: 阿尔泰米西娅·真蒂莱斯基

note.zh:
同一题材前人画过无数次，多半是朱迪斯提着头颅摆姿势。真蒂莱斯基画的是正在进行的动作：两个女人合力把男人按在床上，手腕、肩膀、袖子的方向全部符合真实发力，血呈弧线喷出。

她十七岁时遭老师阿戈斯蒂诺·塔西强奸，在长达七个月的审判中被施以拶刑以「验证证词」。今天很难不把这幅画与那段经历联系起来，但它首先是巴洛克构图与光的教科书——卡拉瓦乔之后最狠的一张。
note.en:
The subject had been painted many times, usually as Judith posing with a head. Gentileschi painted the act: two women pinning a man to a bed, every wrist, shoulder and sleeve aligned with the actual mechanics of force, the blood leaving in arcs.

At seventeen she was raped by her teacher Agostino Tassi and, during a seven-month trial, had her fingers crushed with cords to "verify" her testimony. It is hard not to read the painting through that. But it is first of all a masterclass in Baroque structure and light — the fiercest thing after Caravaggio.

look.zh: 注意两个女人的手腕角度——这是真实的发力方式。
look.en: Look at the angle of both women's wrists. That is how force is actually applied.

src.file: File:Artemisia Gentileschi - Giuditta decapita Oloferne - Google Art Project.jpg

title.en: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp

note.zh:
二十六岁的伦勃朗刚到阿姆斯特丹，靠这张画一举成名。当时的公开解剖是售票的公共事件，每年一次，只能用死刑犯的遗体——台上的人是刚被绞死的抢劫犯阿里斯·金特。

伦勃朗打破了行业惯例：他不让七位外科医生排排看向观众，而是让他们挤成一堆，五个人盯着尸体，两个人望向别处。杜尔博士用镊子提起前臂的屈肌腱，另一只手在空中比划——他正在演示这块肌肉如何让手指弯曲。
note.en:
Rembrandt was twenty-six and newly arrived in Amsterdam; this picture made him. Public dissections were ticketed annual events, and the law allowed only executed criminals — the body is Aris Kindt, hanged that day for armed robbery.

Rembrandt broke the format. Instead of seven surgeons lined up facing the viewer, they crowd into a wedge, five staring at the corpse and two looking elsewhere. Tulp lifts the flexor tendons of the forearm with forceps while his free hand mimes in the air: he is demonstrating how this muscle closes the fingers.

look.zh: 杜尔博士空着的左手正在模仿手指弯曲——他在演示。
look.en: Tulp's free left hand mimes the fingers closing. He is demonstrating.

src.file: File:Rembrandt - The Anatomy Lesson of Dr Nicolaes Tulp.jpg

note.zh:
原名《弗兰斯·班宁·科克上尉的民兵连》。「夜巡」是十九世纪的误称——画面本是白天，只因几百年的清漆氧化发黑才被当成夜景。1940年代清洗后，日光重新显现。

当时的民兵群像通常是排排坐的合影，每人出一份钱、占一样大的位置。伦勃朗把它变成了一个正在启动的瞬间：鼓手擂鼓、狗在吠、长矛斜出画面、一个金衣小女孩闯进人群。这份不守规矩让他失去了一部分委托客户，却造就了荷兰最伟大的一张画。
note.en:
Its real title is The Company of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq. "Night Watch" is a nineteenth-century misreading: the scene is daylight, darkened by centuries of oxidised varnish and only recovered by cleaning in the 1940s.

Militia group portraits were normally rows of equally sized, equally paying faces. Rembrandt turned his into a moment of ignition — a drum starts, a dog barks, pikes cut across the frame, and a small girl in gold light walks straight through the company. The refusal to line them up cost him commissions and produced the greatest painting in the Netherlands.

look.zh: 找那个金衣小女孩：她腰间挂着一只鸡爪，是民兵连徽记的双关。
look.en: Find the girl in gold — the chicken's claws at her waist punningly echo the company's emblem.

src.file: File:The Nightwatch by Rembrandt - Rijksmuseum.jpg

note.zh:
绘画史上最著名的空间谜题。画家本人站在左侧巨大的画布后，正望向我们；小公主玛格丽特被侍女环绕；后墙镜中映出国王与王后的模糊身影——于是「我们」站的位置，正是国王夫妇的位置。

委拉斯开兹把一幅王室肖像变成了关于「观看」本身的作品。福柯在《词与物》开篇用整整一章分析它。画中人物的目光有六七条不同方向，唯有观者被同时纳入画内与画外。
note.en:
The most famous spatial puzzle in painting. The artist stands at the left behind a huge canvas, looking out at us; the Infanta Margarita is surrounded by her maids; and in the mirror on the back wall the king and queen appear as a blur — which means our position is theirs.

Velázquez turned a royal portrait into a work about the act of looking. Foucault opened The Order of Things with a chapter on it. Six or seven separate lines of gaze cross the room, and only the viewer is placed simultaneously inside the picture and outside it.

look.zh: 后墙上那面小镜子——国王与王后只在那里出现。
look.en: The small mirror on the back wall is the only place the king and queen exist.

src.file: File:Las Meninas (1656), by Velazquez.jpg

note.zh:
伦勃朗一生画了约八十幅自画像，是艺术史上最长的自我记录。这一幅作于破产后第三年：房子、藏品、版画收藏全被拍卖，他搬进了租来的小屋。

他没有美化任何东西。眼袋、松弛的下颌、额头的横纹都留着，笔触在暗部几乎变成泥浆，唯有眼睛清亮。晚年的伦勃朗把油彩堆得很厚，用刮刀和笔杆划出纹理——他不再描摹皮肤，而是在造一层皮肤。
note.en:
Rembrandt painted some eighty self-portraits, the longest self-record in art. This one comes three years after his bankruptcy: house, collection and prints all auctioned off, the painter moved into rented rooms.

Nothing is softened. The bagged eyes, the slack jaw, the lined forehead all stay, and the paint in the shadows thickens nearly to mud — only the eyes stay clear. Late Rembrandt built impasto in ridges and scored it with the palette knife and the butt of the brush. He had stopped describing skin and started manufacturing it.

look.zh: 暗部的颜料被刮刀划过——他在造一层皮肤。
look.en: The shadows are scored with a knife. He is building skin, not copying it.

src.file: File:Rembrandt van Rijn - Self-Portrait - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
一个女仆在倒牛奶，仅此而已——但维米尔用画历史画的规格来处理它。她的袖子被日光照成雕塑般的体积，面包壳上的高光是一颗颗独立的白点，近看像浮在表面。

那道从左窗进来的光被反复研究：维米尔可能借助了暗箱（camera obscura），这解释了他画中那种轻微的散焦与光斑。X光显示墙上原本有地图和洗衣篮，他把它们全部抹掉，只留一面空墙和一根钉子。
note.en:
A servant pours milk; that is all. Vermeer treated it with the gravity normally reserved for history painting. Daylight turns her sleeve into sculpture, and the crusts of bread carry beaded highlights that seem to sit on the surface rather than in it.

The light from the left window has been studied endlessly. Vermeer probably used a camera obscura, which would explain the slight defocus and the discs of light. X-rays show a map and a laundry basket on the wall behind her; he painted them all out, leaving bare plaster and one nail.

look.zh: 面包上的高光是一颗颗独立白点，像浮在画面上。
look.en: The highlights on the bread are separate beads of paint, floating on the surface.

src.file: File:Johannes Vermeer - Het melkmeisje - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
普鲁斯特在《追忆似水年华》里让作家贝戈特为了再看一眼这幅画中「那一小块黄色墙面」而死。那块墙确实存在，在画面右侧中段，被阳光照亮，厚厚一层颜料。

维米尔调整了真实的城市轮廓：他压低了近处的建筑，让云的重量占据画面上半。前景的水面几乎不反光，是一整片沉静的暗——荷兰画家很少这样处理河面。全城在等一场刚过去的雨。
note.en:
In Proust, the writer Bergotte dies trying to see once more "the little patch of yellow wall" in this picture. It is real: mid-right, sunlit, laid on thick.

Vermeer adjusted the actual skyline, flattening the near buildings so the weight of cloud could take the upper half. The foreground water barely reflects at all — an unusually still, dark band that Dutch painters rarely allowed themselves. The whole town is waiting out a shower that has just passed.

look.zh: 右侧中段那一小块被照亮的黄墙——普鲁斯特写死了一个人物。
look.en: That small patch of sunlit yellow wall, mid-right, killed a character in Proust.

src.file: File:Vermeer-view-of-delft.jpg

note.zh:
严格说这不是肖像，而是荷兰人所谓的 tronie——一种研究表情与服饰的头像习作，模特身份至今无解。维米尔没有画背景，只留一片深不见底的黑（原本是半透明的绿），于是所有光都落在那张回头的脸上。

那颗「珍珠」其实是两笔白颜料：一笔沉厚的高光，一笔在下缘轻轻带过的反光。近看几乎抽象，退开三步就成了一颗浑圆的珠子。维米尔最惊人的地方，是他知道人眼会替他完成剩下的工作。
note.en:
Strictly speaking this is not a portrait but a tronie — a Dutch study of a head, costume and expression, its sitter unidentified to this day. Vermeer painted no setting at all, only a bottomless dark (originally a translucent green), so every scrap of light lands on the turning face.

The pearl is two touches of white: one loaded highlight, one soft reflection along the lower edge. Up close it is nearly abstract; three steps back it becomes round. Vermeer's real gift was knowing how much the eye will finish for him.

look.zh: 珍珠没有轮廓线——它是被两笔白「暗示」出来的。
look.en: The pearl has no outline. It is implied by two strokes of white.

src.file: File:Meisje met de parel.jpg

title.en: The Return of the Prodigal Son

note.zh:
伦勃朗最后的作品之一，画完不久他就去世了。跪着的儿子光头、赤脚、鞋底磨穿，什么都没剩下；父亲的手落在他背上——左手宽厚有力，右手纤细柔软，一只父亲的手，一只母亲的手。

光只照亮这两个人，其余全部沉入褐色。右侧站着的兄长冷眼旁观，构成了这幅画真正的难题：宽恕是给回来的人的，那么一直没走的人呢？亨利·卢云为它写了一整本书。
note.en:
One of the last things Rembrandt made; he died soon after. The kneeling son is shaven, barefoot, one sole worn through — he has nothing left. The father's hands rest on his back, and they do not match: the left is broad and strong, the right slender and soft. One father's hand, one mother's.

Light falls on these two and nothing else. The elder brother stands at the right, watching coldly, and poses the real problem of the picture: forgiveness is for the one who came back — what about the one who never left? Henri Nouwen wrote an entire book about it.

look.zh: 父亲的两只手不一样：一只男性，一只女性。
look.en: The father's two hands differ: one masculine, one feminine.

src.file: File:Rembrandt Harmensz van Rijn - Return of the Prodigal Son - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
一匹真人大小的赛马，没有背景、没有骑手、没有马厩——十八世纪的动物画里，这种彻底的留白闻所未闻。有传说称原计划要加上乔治三世的骑像，被斯塔布斯拒绝。

他的解剖学功底来自一段骇人的经历：1756年他在乡下租了一间农舍，把马的尸体吊起来逐层解剖，画了十八个月，出版了《马的解剖》。这幅画里每一块肌肉的走向都经得起兽医的检验。
note.en:
A life-size racehorse with no background, no rider and no stable — a degree of emptiness unheard of in eighteenth-century animal painting. Tradition says a mounted George III was planned for the canvas and Stubbs refused.

His anatomy came from a grim apprenticeship: in 1756 he rented a farmhouse, suspended horse carcasses and dissected them layer by layer for eighteen months, publishing The Anatomy of the Horse. Every muscle here would satisfy a veterinarian.

look.zh: 没有背景、没有骑手——1762年，这是激进的。
look.en: No background, no rider. In 1762 that was radical.

src.file: File:Whistlejacket by George Stubbs.jpg

note.zh:
洛可可最著名的一张画，也是一份露骨的委托。据说赞助人要求：画我的情妇荡秋千，让一位主教推她，而我躺在能看见她裙下的位置。弗拉戈纳尔照办了，只把主教换成了丈夫。

她踢飞的鞋在空中，左下角灌木里的年轻人伸着手；左侧的丘比特雕像把手指按在唇上——「别说出去」。整幅画的光像舞台追光，只打在她粉色的裙子上，四周花园暗成一团。
note.en:
The most famous Rococo painting, and a candid commission. The patron reportedly asked for his mistress on a swing, pushed by a bishop, with himself placed to see up her skirts. Fragonard obliged, demoting the bishop to a husband.

Her shoe flies off; a young man in the shrubbery at lower left reaches up; and the Cupid statue on the left presses a finger to his lips — say nothing. The light works like a stage spot, hitting only the pink dress while the garden sinks into darkness.

look.zh: 左边的丘比特把手指按在唇上——这是全画唯一的道德评论。
look.en: Cupid, on the left, presses a finger to his lips. That is the picture's only moral comment.

src.file: File:Fragonard, The Swing.jpg

museum.zh: 亨廷顿图书馆与艺术馆

note.zh:
根兹博罗的对手雷诺兹曾在皇家美术学院讲课时说，冷色（尤其是蓝）绝不应占据画面主体。根兹博罗的回应就是这张几乎全蓝的画——一次礼貌但毫不含糊的反驳。

少年穿的是十七世纪的凡·戴克式服装，不是当时的时装；这是向英国肖像画祖师的致敬。X光显示画布下还有另一幅未完成的男子肖像。1922年它被卖到美国，离开英国时伦敦国家美术馆为它举行了告别展。
note.en:
Gainsborough's rival Reynolds told the Royal Academy that cool colours, blue above all, must never dominate a canvas. Gainsborough's reply was this almost entirely blue painting — polite, and unmistakable.

The boy wears seventeenth-century Van Dyck costume rather than contemporary dress, a salute to the founding father of English portraiture. X-rays reveal an unfinished portrait of a man beneath. When it was sold to America in 1922 the National Gallery in London held a farewell exhibition.

look.zh: 这是一次反驳：当时的权威说蓝色不能主导画面。
look.en: This is an argument. The reigning authority had said blue must never dominate.

src.file: File:Thomas Gainsborough - The Blue Boy (1770).jpg

note.zh:
维热·勒布伦是玛丽·安托瓦内特的御用肖像画家，一生画了六百多幅肖像。这幅自画像改编自鲁本斯的《草帽》，她在安特卫普见到原作后深受震动，回来立刻重画了一版属于自己的。

她把画室的封闭光线换成了户外直射光——脸的一半在草帽的阴影里，一半被日光照亮，这在1780年代是罕见的大胆。她手持调色板，直视观者，神情从容：一位职业画家在宣布自己的身份。法国大革命爆发后她流亡欧洲十二年。
note.en:
Vigée Le Brun was Marie Antoinette's portraitist and painted more than six hundred portraits. This self-portrait reworks Rubens's Chapeau de Paille, which she saw in Antwerp and which stunned her; she went home and made her own version at once.

She swapped enclosed studio light for direct sun — half the face in the hat's shadow, half in daylight — an unusual risk in the 1780s. She holds her palette, meets our eye, and looks entirely at ease: a professional announcing her profession. When the Revolution came she spent twelve years in exile.

look.zh: 她手持调色板直视观者——这是一份职业声明。
look.en: Palette in hand, meeting your eye: a statement of profession.

src.file: File:Élisabeth Louise Vigée Le Brun (1755–1842) Self-Portrait in a Straw Hat, after 1782.jpg

note.zh:
新古典主义的宣言。洛可可的曲线、粉色和轻佻在这里被一刀切断：三道直线般的手臂、三个笔直的拱、一块空荡荡的石地。大卫在罗马画完它，运回巴黎时轰动一时。

左侧男人全是直线与角度，右侧女人全是曲线与瘫软——性别被编码成了几何。五年后法国大革命爆发，这幅画被追认为革命精神的先声，尽管大卫画它时只是想画一个罗马故事。
note.en:
The manifesto of Neoclassicism. Rococo's curves, pinks and frivolity are cut off in one stroke: three arms like straight lines, three plain arches, an empty stone floor. David painted it in Rome and its arrival in Paris caused a sensation.

Everything male on the left is line and angle; everything female on the right is curve and collapse — gender encoded as geometry. Five years later the Revolution began and the picture was retroactively claimed as its herald, though David had set out only to paint a Roman story.

look.zh: 左边全是直线，右边全是曲线——构图本身在讲性别。
look.en: Straight lines on the left, curves on the right. The composition argues about gender.

src.file: File:Jacques-Louis David, Le Serment des Horaces.jpg

museum.en: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

note.zh:
革命领袖马拉被夏洛特·科黛刺杀于浴缸中，大卫在两天后开始作画。他把现场清空了：真实的房间挂满地图与武器，画里只剩一块空白的墙——上半幅什么都没有，像一座墓碑。

马拉患有皮肤病，必须终日浸在药浴里办公；大卫抹去了皮肤的溃烂，让他的身体呈现出基督下十字架般的姿态。木箱上刻着「献给马拉，大卫」。这是政治宣传，也是欧洲绘画史上最有效的一次。
note.en:
Marat was stabbed in his bath by Charlotte Corday; David began painting two days later. He emptied the room. The real one was hung with maps and weapons; here the upper half of the canvas is bare wall, like a headstone.

Marat's skin disease forced him to work submerged in medicated water. David erased the lesions and arranged the body in the posture of a Deposition. The packing crate is inscribed "À MARAT, DAVID." It is propaganda, and the most effective in the history of European painting.

look.zh: 画面上半部什么都没有——那片空白就是墓碑。
look.en: The top half of the canvas is empty. That blankness is the tombstone.

src.file: File:Jacques-Louis David - Marat assassinated - Google Art Project 2.jpg

note.zh:
现代战争画的起点。此前的战争题材总在歌颂英雄，戈雅第一次把镜头对准被处决的一方：拿破仑军队在马德里郊外枪杀起义者，行刑队没有面孔，只有一排背影和枪管。

光源是地上那盏方形提灯，它把白衬衫的男人照成整幅画唯一的亮点。他双臂张开——右掌上有一道钉痕般的暗影。戈雅没有画英雄的从容，他画的是恐惧本身。马奈的《枪决马克西米连》、毕加索的《格尔尼卡》都从这里出发。
note.en:
The starting point of modern war painting. Battle pictures had celebrated heroes; Goya turned the picture around to face the executed. Napoleon's troops shoot Madrid insurgents outside the city, and the firing squad has no faces — only a row of backs and barrels.

The light source is the square lantern on the ground, which makes the man in the white shirt the single bright thing in the painting. His arms are thrown open, and there is a nail-dark mark on the right palm. Goya did not paint heroic composure; he painted fear. Manet's Execution of Maximilian and Picasso's Guernica both begin here.

look.zh: 看他右手掌心的暗影——戈雅在暗示钉痕。
look.en: Look at the shadow in his right palm. Goya is suggesting a stigma.

src.file: File:El Tres de Mayo, by Francisco de Goya, from Prado thin black margin.jpg

note.zh:
1819年沙龙展出时被批评家嘲笑：「她多了三节脊椎。」这不是失误。安格尔故意拉长背部、错置骨盆、把右臂画得不合解剖——为了让身体成为一条不中断的曲线。

后来的研究者数过，若按真实比例，她的腰椎确实多出两到三节。安格尔的回答是：线条比骨头重要。二十世纪的现代主义者反而在这里找到了同类——毕加索说，变形从安格尔就开始了。
note.en:
Mocked at the 1819 Salon: "she has three vertebrae too many." It was not a mistake. Ingres deliberately lengthened the back, displaced the pelvis and gave the right arm an impossible anatomy so the body could run as one unbroken curve.

Later analysts counted: at true proportions she carries two or three extra lumbar vertebrae. Ingres's answer was that line matters more than bone. Twentieth-century modernists recognised a relative — Picasso said distortion began with Ingres.

look.zh: 她的脊椎比常人多两三节——安格尔知道，他不在乎。
look.en: She has two or three vertebrae too many. Ingres knew, and did not care.

src.file: File:Jean Auguste Dominique Ingres, La Grande Odalisque, 1814.jpg

title.en: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog

artist.zh: 卡斯帕·大卫·弗里德里希

note.zh:
德国浪漫主义的象征。弗里德里希用了一个后来被无数次模仿的构图：主角背对我们，站在画面正中，于是观者不是在看他，而是站进了他的身体里，替他看那片雾。

地质学家考证过，这些岩石来自萨克森的易北砂岩山，但被弗里德里希拆散重组成了一处并不存在的地点。雾遮住了山谷，也遮住了道路——浪漫主义关心的从来不是风景，而是人在无限面前那种既渺小又亢奋的心情。
note.en:
The emblem of German Romanticism. Friedrich used a device copied endlessly since: the figure turns his back, dead centre, so we do not look at him — we stand inside him and look at the fog on his behalf.

Geologists have identified the rocks as Elbe Sandstone formations in Saxony, dismantled and reassembled by Friedrich into a place that does not exist. The fog hides the valley and hides the way down. Romanticism was never really about landscape; it was about how a person feels, small and exhilarated at once, in front of the infinite.

look.zh: 没有一条路通向山下——这是有意的。
look.en: There is no path down. That is deliberate.

src.file: File:Caspar David Friedrich - Wanderer above the sea of fog.jpg

note.zh:
1816年，法国护卫舰梅杜萨号因指挥无能触礁，147人被丢在一只临时木筏上漂流十三天，获救时仅剩十五人，期间发生过同类相食。籍里柯二十七岁，为此走访幸存者、去医院画尸体、在工作室搭了一座木筏模型。

他放弃了「获救」的高光时刻，选了更残酷的一秒：远处地平线上有一个几乎看不见的小点，那是救援船——而它正在驶离。整幅画由两个三角构成，一个由尸体堆起，一个由挥舞的衣衫指向那个渺茫的希望。
note.en:
In 1816 the French frigate Méduse ran aground through incompetence and 147 people were abandoned on an improvised raft. Thirteen days later fifteen were alive; cannibalism had occurred. Géricault was twenty-seven. He interviewed survivors, drew corpses in hospitals, and built a model raft in his studio.

He rejected the moment of rescue for something crueller: on the horizon there is an almost invisible speck — the rescue ship, sailing away. The composition is two triangles, one built from bodies, one from waving cloth pointing at a hope that is receding.

look.zh: 右上角地平线上那个小点，就是正在驶远的救援船。
look.en: That speck on the horizon at upper right is the ship — and it is leaving.

src.file: File:JEAN LOUIS THÉODORE GÉRICAULT - La Balsa de la Medusa (Museo del Louvre, 1818-19).jpg

note.zh:
画的是萨福克郡弗拉特福德的一处浅滩，康斯太勃尔父亲的磨坊就在附近。他一生几乎只画自己长大的这几平方英里，说「我熟悉的这些地方让我成为画家」。

英国人当时嫌它太粗糙，1824年这张画在巴黎沙龙展出，却让德拉克洛瓦大受震动，据说回去重画了自己作品的背景。康斯太勃尔在暗部大量点上白色高光（时人讥为「康斯太勃尔的雪」），正是这种湿润的闪烁，预示了印象派。
note.en:
A shallow ford at Flatford in Suffolk, close to the mill owned by Constable's father. He painted almost nothing but the few square miles he grew up in: "these scenes made me a painter."

The English found it coarse. Shown at the Paris Salon in 1824, it shook Delacroix, who is said to have gone home and repainted his own backgrounds. Constable flecked white highlights across his shadows — critics called it "Constable's snow" — and that damp glitter is where Impressionism starts.

look.zh: 暗部里那些白点不是脏——是水汽反光，当年被嘲笑为「康斯太勃尔的雪」。
look.en: Those white flecks in the shadows are moisture, not dirt. Critics called them Constable's snow.

src.file: File:John Constable The Hay Wain.jpg

medium.zh: 壁上混合材料，后移至布面
medium.en: Mixed media mural, transferred to canvas

note.zh:
「黑色绘画」之一。晚年的戈雅失聪、隐居在马德里郊外的「聋人之家」，直接在自家墙壁上画了十四幅从不打算示人的画，这是其中最骇人的一幅。

他没有画古典神话里那个威严的农神，而是画了一个眼睛暴突、精神崩溃的老人，正在啃食一具已经没有头的身体。戈雅死后半个世纪，这些壁画被剥离转到画布上，转移过程中损失了部分内容——包括萨图恩下体原有的一段。
note.en:
One of the Black Paintings. Deaf and withdrawn, Goya covered the walls of his house outside Madrid with fourteen pictures he never intended anyone to see. This is the most appalling of them.

He did not paint the stately Saturn of classical myth but a wild-eyed old man in psychotic collapse, eating a body that has already lost its head. Half a century after Goya's death the murals were stripped from the plaster and transferred to canvas, losing material in the process — including part of Saturn's lower body.

look.zh: 这画本挂在戈雅自家餐厅的墙上，从未打算给人看。
look.en: This hung on the wall of Goya's own dining room. It was never meant to be seen.

src.file: File:Francisco de Goya, Saturno devorando a su hijo (1819-1823).jpg

note.zh:
纪念1830年七月革命。德拉克洛瓦给弟弟写信说：「我虽然没有为祖国战斗，至少可以为她作画。」画中的自由女神不是古典雕像式的神祇，她赤足、腋下有汗毛、衣裙脏污——一个真实的女人被抬上了寓言的位置。

她身边的人群构成一个横跨阶级的三角：戴高礼帽的资产者、持刀的工人、举双枪的少年。脚下的尸体不分敌我。远处巴黎圣母院的塔楼在硝烟里若隐若现。这幅画长期被政府认为过于煽动，多年不得公开展出。
note.en:
Painted for the July Revolution of 1830. Delacroix wrote to his brother: "If I have not fought for my country, at least I shall paint for her." His Liberty is not a classical deity — she is barefoot, her underarms unshaved, her dress soiled: a real woman raised into allegory.

The crowd behind her forms a triangle across the classes: a bourgeois in a top hat, a worker with a sabre, a boy with two pistols. The dead at their feet belong to both sides. The towers of Notre-Dame surface faintly through the smoke. Successive governments judged the picture too inflammatory and kept it out of public view for years.

look.zh: 戴高礼帽的男人常被误认为德拉克洛瓦自己——他其实代表资产阶级。
look.en: The man in the top hat is often mistaken for Delacroix; he stands for the bourgeoisie.

src.file: File:Eugène Delacroix - Le 28 Juillet. La Liberté guidant le peuple.jpg

museum.zh: 多家馆藏（大都会艺术博物馆等）

note.zh:
《富岳三十六景》的第一图。北斋当时七十出头，用的是刚从荷兰进口的「普鲁士蓝」——这种化学合成颜料让浮世绘第一次能印出如此深沉稳定的蓝，也让这幅画有了现代感。

三条渔船夹在浪谷里，船夫伏身不动；远处的富士山被前景的浪爪压成一个小小的白三角。真正的主角不是山，是那一瞬间即将崩塌的水。梵高见过它，德彪西把它印在《大海》的乐谱封面上。
note.en:
The opening sheet of Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. Hokusai was past seventy and working with Prussian blue, a synthetic pigment newly imported through Dutch traders — the first time a woodblock print could hold a blue this deep and this stable.

Three boats are trapped in the trough, their crews flattened against the hulls, while Fuji is reduced to a small white triangle beneath the wave's claw. The mountain is not the subject; the instant before collapse is. Van Gogh saw it, and Debussy put it on the cover of La Mer.

look.zh: 找一找富士山——它小得像浪花的一部分，这正是北斋的玩笑。
look.en: Find Fuji: it is small enough to read as another crest. That is Hokusai's joke.

src.file: File:Tsunami by hokusai 19th century.jpg

note.zh:
《富岳三十六景》中最简的一幅，也是最难印的一幅。整座山只由三块色面构成：赭红的山体、深绿的林带、留白的残雪。天空的蓝要从顶部向下渐淡，全靠印工手工擦拭色版，每一张成品的浓淡都不同。

「凯风」指初秋南风。晴日清晨，富士山在特定条件下会短暂泛出赤红，这是真实存在的现象。北斋没有加任何人物——三十六景里，这是极少数只有山的一幅。
note.en:
The simplest sheet in Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, and the hardest to print. The mountain is three flat fields: ochre-red slope, dark green forest, unprinted white snow. The blue sky must fade from the top edge downward, which the printer achieved by wiping the block by hand — so no two impressions are quite alike.

"Fine wind" means the southerly of early autumn. On clear mornings under the right conditions Fuji really does flush red for a short time. Hokusai added no figures: among the thirty-six views, this is one of the very few that is only the mountain.

look.zh: 天空的渐变靠印工手工擦色——每一张都不一样。
look.en: The sky gradient was wiped by hand at the press. No two prints match.

src.file: File:Red Fuji southern wind clear morning.jpg

title.zh: 被拖去解体的战舰无畏号

note.zh:
透纳自称这是他「最钟爱的作品」，晚年拒绝出售。画的是1838年的真实事件：特拉法加海战的功勋舰无畏号，被一艘冒黑烟的蒸汽拖船拽向泰晤士河边的拆船厂。

他动了手脚：真实的拖运在白天进行，桅杆早已拆除。透纳把它改成了日落，让苍白如幽灵的帆船与黑色矮壮的拖船并置，太阳沉在右边，新月已在左边升起。一个时代被另一个时代拖走——十九世纪最伤感的一张画。
note.en:
Turner called it his "darling" and refused to sell it in later life. The event was real: in 1838 the Temeraire, a hero of Trafalgar, was towed up the Thames to the breakers by a steam tug.

He altered the facts. The real tow happened in daylight and the masts had already been removed. Turner moved it to sunset and set a pale, ghostly sailing ship beside a squat black tug, sun sinking on the right, new moon already up on the left. One age hauling another away — the most elegiac painting of the nineteenth century.

look.zh: 左边已经升起新月，右边太阳未落——两个时代同框。
look.en: A new moon on the left, the sun not yet down on the right: two eras in one frame.

src.file: File:The Fighting Temeraire, JMW Turner, National Gallery.jpg

title.zh: 雨、蒸汽和速度——大西部铁路

note.zh:
六十九岁的透纳画蒸汽机车冲过泰晤士河上的梅登黑德铁路桥。传说他曾在暴雨中把头伸出车窗九分钟，只为记住那种感觉。

形体几乎全部溶解，只有锅炉口一点黑与桥墩的直线还抓得住。左下角有一只野兔在铁轨前奔跑——它跑不过火车。这是英国绘画里第一次，工业不再是风景的入侵者，而成了风景本身。莫奈流亡伦敦时看过透纳，印象派的门由此打开。
note.en:
Turner at sixty-nine, painting a locomotive crossing Maidenhead Railway Bridge over the Thames. The story goes that he leaned out of a carriage window in a downpour for nine minutes to fix the sensation.

Form has almost entirely dissolved; only the black mouth of the firebox and the straight piers still hold. In the lower left a hare runs ahead of the train, and it will not outrun it. This is the first time in British painting that industry stops invading the landscape and becomes it. Monet saw Turner during his London exile, and Impressionism walked through the door.

look.zh: 轨道前方有一只野兔——它是被速度追赶的旧世界。
look.en: A hare runs ahead of the engine: the old world, being outpaced.

src.file: File:Rain Steam and Speed the Great Western Railway.jpg

note.zh:
美国最著名的历史画，却是一位德裔画家在杜塞尔多夫画的——洛伊茨想用美国革命鼓舞1848年的欧洲革命者。第一版毁于工作室火灾，这是第二版。

历史学家指出的错误很多：星条旗当时尚未采用、渡河在深夜而非黎明、船型不对、没人会在冰河上站着。但洛伊茨要的不是准确，是姿态。船上的人来自不同族裔与阶层，那是他心中的共和国。
note.en:
America's most famous history painting was made in Düsseldorf by a German artist: Leutze meant it to encourage the European revolutionaries of 1848. The first version burned in his studio; this is the second.

Historians list the errors freely — that flag did not yet exist, the crossing happened in darkness rather than at dawn, the boat is the wrong type, and nobody stands up in an ice-choked river. Leutze was not after accuracy but posture. The men in the boat come from different races and classes: that was his republic.

look.zh: 画中的星条旗当时还没被采用——洛伊茨要的是姿态，不是准确。
look.en: That flag did not exist yet. Leutze wanted the pose, not the facts.

src.file: File:Washington Crossing the Delaware by Emanuel Leutze, MMA-NYC, 1851.jpg

note.zh:
《哈姆雷特》里奥菲莉娅溺水的一幕。米莱先在萨里郡霍格斯米尔河边露天画了五个月的植物，每一株都可辨认，且都对应莎剧或维多利亚花语：柳树是被弃之爱，荨麻是痛苦，雏菊是天真，罂粟是死亡。

模特伊丽莎白·西德尔躺在画室的浴缸里摆姿，缸下用油灯保温；灯灭了，她着凉重病，她父亲向米莱索赔医药费。她后来成了罗塞蒂的妻子与缪斯。
note.en:
Ophelia's drowning from Hamlet. Millais spent five months painting the plants outdoors along the Hogsmill in Surrey; every species is identifiable and every one carries meaning from the play or Victorian flower language — willow for forsaken love, nettle for pain, daisy for innocence, poppy for death.

The model, Elizabeth Siddal, posed in a bath in his studio, warmed by lamps underneath. The lamps went out, she fell seriously ill, and her father sent Millais the doctor's bill. She later became Rossetti's wife and muse.

look.zh: 水面每一株植物都能查到名字，也都有含义。
look.en: Every plant on the water is identifiable — and every one means something.

src.file: File:John Everett Millais - Ophelia - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
博纳尔为了写生，向巴黎警方申请了「男装许可证」——十九世纪的法国女性穿裤子需要官方批准。她每周两次去巴黎的马市，混在马贩子中间画了一年半。

五米长的画布上，佩尔什马群沿对角线狂奔，尘土、鬃毛与肌肉全在运动。这幅画让她成为当时全欧洲最著名、收入最高的女画家，维多利亚女王专门要求私下观看。她与两位女性伴侣先后共同生活了几十年，从不解释。
note.en:
To work from life Bonheur applied to the Paris police for a permit to wear men's clothing — legally required for a Frenchwoman in trousers. Twice a week for a year and a half she drew at the horse market among the dealers.

Across five metres of canvas the Percherons surge along a diagonal, dust, manes and muscle all in motion. The picture made her the most famous and best-paid woman painter in Europe; Queen Victoria asked for a private viewing. She lived for decades with two successive female partners and never explained herself.

look.zh: 她申请了官方「男装许可」才能进马市写生。
look.en: She needed an official permit to wear trousers into the horse market.

src.file: File:Rosa Bonheur, The Horse Fair, 1852–55.jpg

note.zh:
《名所江户百景》之一。广重把一根梅枝放到极近的前景，几乎贴着观者的脸，游人则缩到远处的绿地里——这种「近大远小到失衡」的裁切，在当时的欧洲绘画中完全没有先例。

梵高在巴黎见到它，直接临摹了一幅油画版《日本趣味：梅花》，还在画面两侧抄了一些他看不懂的汉字。他在信里说：「我们全都在向日本人学习。」
note.en:
From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo. Hiroshige pushed a plum branch into the extreme foreground, almost against the viewer's face, and shrank the visitors into a green field far behind — a cropping so unbalanced that European painting had no precedent for it.

Van Gogh saw the print in Paris and copied it in oil as Japonaiserie: Flowering Plum Tree, adding columns of Chinese characters down each side that he could not read. "We all learn from the Japanese," he wrote.

look.zh: 前景那根梅枝几乎贴在你脸上——梵高临摹过这张。
look.en: That branch is almost against your face. Van Gogh copied this print in oil.

src.file: File:De pruimenboomgaard te Kameido-Rijksmuseum RP-P-1956-743.jpeg

title.en: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge and Atake

note.zh:
《名所江户百景》中最著名的一张。雨是用极细的直线刻版印成的，两组方向略有差异的雨线交叠，产生了真正倾盆的错觉——在木版上刻出这样的细线，是技术上的绝技。

桥上的人各自弓身奔跑，有人举着蓑衣，有人合撑一把伞；下方的木筏工在雨里毫无遮蔽。远岸完全消失在灰色里。梵高在1887年临摹了这张画，是他最忠实的一次临摹。
note.en:
The most famous sheet in One Hundred Famous Views of Edo. The rain is cut as extremely fine straight lines, in two overlapping sets at slightly different angles, producing a genuine downpour — carving lines that fine into a woodblock is a feat in itself.

On the bridge people run bent over, one holding a straw cape overhead, two sharing an umbrella; below, a raftsman has no cover at all. The far bank has dissolved into grey. Van Gogh copied this print in oil in 1887, his most faithful copy of anything.

look.zh: 雨是两组角度略不同的细线叠印而成——木刻的绝技。
look.en: The rain is two sets of hair-fine lines at different angles: a feat of block-cutting.

src.file: File:Hiroshige, Sudden shower over Shin-Ōhashi bridge and Atake, 1857.jpg

note.zh:
1865年沙龙上引发的骚动大到要派警卫看守。观众能接受裸体女神，不能接受一个直视他们的巴黎妓女：她脖子上系着黑丝带，脚上还穿着拖鞋，手不是遮掩而是按住。

构图直接搬自提香的《乌尔比诺的维纳斯》，这是有意的挑衅。马奈把柔和的明暗过渡全部压平，人体像贴在画面上的一张剪影——批评家说她「像扑克牌上的皇后」。二十世纪的现代绘画从这张平面性开始。
note.en:
The uproar at the 1865 Salon was severe enough to require guards. Viewers could accept a nude goddess; they could not accept a Parisian prostitute looking back at them, a black ribbon at her throat, one slipper still on, her hand not concealing but pressing down.

The composition is lifted from Titian's Venus of Urbino, and the theft is the point. Manet flattened every soft transition until the body reads as a cut-out laid on the surface — a critic said she looked like the queen on a playing card. Modern painting's flatness starts here.

look.zh: 她的手不是遮掩，是「按住」——这是当年真正激怒观众的地方。
look.en: Her hand does not conceal; it presses down. That is what actually enraged the Salon.

src.file: File:Edouard Manet - Olympia - Google Art Project 3.jpg

note.zh:
被1863年官方沙龙拒收，转而在拿破仑三世特设的「落选者沙龙」展出，成为整场展览的丑闻中心。问题不在裸体，而在语境：两个穿着当代西装的男人，一个赤裸的当代女人，在真实的树林里野餐。

三人姿势取自拉斐尔学生的一幅版画。马奈几乎取消了中间调，人物边缘生硬，后景那个洗浴的女人比例明显过大——这些「错误」是宣言：绘画首先是平面上的颜料。
note.en:
Rejected by the 1863 Salon and shown instead at the Salon des Refusés that Napoleon III set up in response, where it became the scandal of the exhibition. The problem was not nudity but context: two men in contemporary suits, one naked contemporary woman, a picnic in a real wood.

The grouping derives from an engraving after Raphael. Manet nearly eliminated the middle tones, hardened every contour, and left the bathing woman behind them conspicuously too large. Those "errors" are the argument: painting is pigment on a flat surface first.

look.zh: 后景洗浴的女人比例明显太大——马奈故意留着这个「错误」。
look.en: The bather behind is plainly too large. Manet left the "error" on purpose.

src.file: File:Edouard Manet - Luncheon on the Grass - Google Art Project.jpg

title.zh: 灰与黑的排列 第一号（画家的母亲）
title.en: Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1

artist.zh: 詹姆斯·麦克尼尔·惠斯勒

note.zh:
惠斯勒坚持这不是肖像，标题只谈颜色：「对公众来说，这是不是我母亲有什么要紧？」他要的是灰与黑之间的音程关系，人物只是一个形状。

然而它偏偏成了母性的国民图腾——1934年美国发行了印有此画的邮票，加上「纪念与致敬美国母亲」的字样，正是惠斯勒最反对的读法。构图极端简化：一道墙、一幅版画、一块帘子、一个直角坐姿的侧影。
note.en:
Whistler insisted it was not a portrait; the title speaks only of colour. "What can or ought the public care about the identity of the portrait?" He wanted the interval between grey and black, and the sitter is a shape.

It became the national icon of motherhood anyway — in 1934 the United States printed it on a stamp captioned "In memory and in honor of the mothers of America," precisely the reading he had refused. The composition is stripped to a wall, a framed print, a curtain, and a profile seated at right angles.

look.zh: 惠斯勒说这只是关于灰与黑的关系，与母亲无关。
look.en: Whistler said it was about grey and black, not about his mother.

src.file: File:Whistlers Mother high res.jpg

note.zh:
「印象派」这个名字就来自这张画。1874年首次群展，评论家路易·勒鲁瓦以此题写了一篇嘲讽文章《印象主义者的展览》，把「未完成的草稿」当作罪状。这群画家索性接受了这个绰号。

画的是勒阿弗尔港的清晨薄雾。有意思的是那轮橙红的太阳：它的亮度与周围灰蓝的雾气几乎完全相同——把画面转成黑白，太阳会当场消失。莫奈画的不是太阳，是我们看见太阳时的那种颤动。
note.en:
Impressionism takes its name from this canvas. At the group's first exhibition in 1874, the critic Louis Leroy used the title for a mocking review, treating an unfinished-looking sketch as an offence. The painters adopted the insult as a banner.

The subject is dawn mist over the harbour at Le Havre. The remarkable thing is the orange sun: its luminance is almost identical to the grey-blue haze around it, so convert the image to greyscale and the sun vanishes. Monet did not paint the sun; he painted the vibration of seeing one.

look.zh: 眯起眼睛——太阳会融进雾里，因为它们一样亮。
look.en: Squint: the sun dissolves into the haze. They are the same brightness.

src.file: File:Claude Monet, Impression, soleil levant.jpg

note.zh:
1874年第一届印象派展览上的作品，画的是莫里索的姐姐艾德玛与刚出生的外甥女。当时女性画家几乎无法进入公共空间写生，她的题材因此集中在家庭内部——限制被她转化成了专长。

最精彩的是那层白纱：几乎透明，笔触松散得像随手扫过，却把孩子隔在另一个世界。母亲的手撑着头，眼神专注中带着疲惫。这是艺术史上少有的、由一位母亲从内部观看的母性图像。
note.en:
Shown at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874: Morisot's sister Edma with her newborn daughter. Women painters could barely work in public spaces, so her subjects sat indoors — and she turned the restriction into a speciality.

The best passage is the veil: almost transparent, brushed so loosely it looks casual, and yet it holds the child in a separate world. The mother's hand props her head; her attention is total and tired. This is one of the rare images of motherhood in art seen from inside it, by a mother.

look.zh: 那层白纱几乎是透明的——却把母子分在两个世界。
look.en: The veil is nearly transparent, and it still separates the two of them.

src.file: File:Berthe Morisot - The Cradle - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
德加画了一千五百多件与芭蕾有关的作品，却几乎从不画演出。他画的是排练、等待、系鞋带、抓背、打哈欠——舞台之外的劳动。

这一幅里，老教师佩罗拄杖站在中央，一个女孩正在完成动作，其余人在走神。地板的透视被拉得很陡，人物顺着这道斜坡向后退去。十九世纪巴黎歌剧院的芭蕾女孩多来自贫困家庭，德加没有美化这一点：他画的是一份工作。
note.en:
Degas made more than fifteen hundred works about ballet and almost never painted a performance. He painted rehearsal, waiting, tying shoes, scratching a back, yawning — the labour offstage.

Here the old ballet master Perrot stands with his stick at the centre, one girl completes a step, and everyone else has drifted. The floor is raked steeply in perspective and the figures recede up its slope. The Opéra's dancers came largely from poor families, and Degas does not prettify it: he is painting a job.

look.zh: 没有人在跳舞——她们在等、在挠背、在走神。
look.en: Nobody is dancing. They are waiting, scratching, drifting.

src.file: File:Edgar Degas - The Ballet Class - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
画的是莫奈的第一任妻子卡米耶与七岁的儿子让。视角极低，几乎是仰躺在草坡上看她——她于是顶着整片天空，裙摆与面纱被风向同一侧吹开。

脸在阳伞的阴影里几乎没有五官，只用几笔带过。莫奈关心的是逆光：阳伞下方的绿色反光、白裙上的蓝紫阴影、草丛里跳动的红点。四年后卡米耶病逝，年仅三十二岁。
note.en:
Monet's first wife Camille with their seven-year-old son Jean. The viewpoint is very low, as if lying back on the slope, so she carries the whole sky, skirt and veil blown to one side by a single gust.

Her face, in the parasol's shadow, has almost no features — a few strokes and nothing more. What interested Monet was contre-jour: green light bouncing under the parasol, blue-violet shadow on white cloth, red flickering through the grass. Camille died four years later, aged thirty-two.

look.zh: 她的脸几乎没有五官——莫奈只在画光。
look.en: Her face has almost no features. Monet is painting only the light.

src.file: File:Claude Monet - Woman with a Parasol - Madame Monet and Her Son - Google Art Project.jpg

title.en: Bal du moulin de la Galette

artist.zh: 皮埃尔-奥古斯特·雷诺阿

note.zh:
蒙马特高地上一家露天舞场的周日下午。雷诺阿在附近租了工作室，每天让朋友把这张一米七的画布搬到现场，坚持在户外完成——印象派对「实地作画」的执念到了近乎荒谬的地步。

最动人的是穿过树叶洒下的光斑：它们落在人们的肩膀、帽檐、地面上，形状模糊、边缘发紫。同时代的批评家说画中人像「长了霉」。今天我们知道，那正是阳光穿过树冠时真实的样子。
note.en:
A Sunday afternoon at an open-air dance hall on Montmartre. Renoir rented a studio nearby and had friends carry this metre-and-three-quarter canvas to the site daily so it could be finished outdoors — Impressionist insistence on painting from life taken to an almost absurd extreme.

The best thing in it is the dappled light falling through leaves onto shoulders, hat brims and gravel, blurred at the edges and tinged violet. Critics said the figures looked mouldy. We now know that is exactly what sunlight through a canopy does.

look.zh: 衣服上那些紫色斑块是树影——当年被讥为「发霉」。
look.en: Those violet patches on the clothes are leaf shadow. Critics called it mould.

src.file: File:Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Le Moulin de la Galette.jpg

note.zh:
1893年在伦敦展出时引发道德恐慌，被斥为「堕落」「丑陋」，报纸争论了好几周。今天看，它的激进之处在构图：整个左下角被空白的桌面占据，两个人被推到右上角，中间没有任何东西连接他们。

德加借用了日本浮世绘和摄影的裁切方式——桌角切断、人物被边框吃掉一半。女子的目光垂着，脚尖朝外；男人望向画外。他们同桌而坐，却分属两个世界。
note.en:
Shown in London in 1893, it caused a moral panic — "degraded," "ugly" — and the papers argued for weeks. What is actually radical is the composition: the lower left is given over to empty tabletop, the two figures are shoved into the upper right, and nothing connects them.

Degas borrowed his cropping from Japanese prints and from photography: table corners run off, figures are eaten by the frame. Her eyes are down and her feet turn away; he looks out of the picture entirely. Same table, different worlds.

look.zh: 左下角大片空桌面——德加用「空」来表达疏离。
look.en: That expanse of empty table at lower left is how Degas paints estrangement.

src.file: File:Edgar Degas - In a Café - Google Art Project 2.jpg

note.zh:
奥斯曼男爵改造后的新巴黎：笔直的大道、统一的立面、湿漉漉的石板路。卡耶博特出身富裕工程师家庭，用近乎制图般的透视处理街口——正中那盏路灯把画面精确地一分为二。

他不像别的印象派那样把形体化开，反而画得极其锐利。人物彼此不看、不说话，前景那对男女正要走出画外，与我们擦身而过。这是最早的一批「现代都市孤独」图像之一。

卡耶博特也是印象派最重要的赞助人，他的遗赠构成了今天奥赛博物馆的核心。
note.en:
Haussmann's rebuilt Paris: straight boulevards, uniform façades, wet stone. Caillebotte came from a wealthy engineering family and handled the junction with almost draughtsman's perspective — the lamp post at the centre divides the canvas exactly in two.

Unlike his Impressionist colleagues he did not dissolve form; he sharpened it. No one looks at anyone, no one speaks, and the couple in front are about to walk out of the picture past us. It is one of the earliest images of modern urban solitude.

Caillebotte was also Impressionism's key patron; his bequest forms the core of the Musée d'Orsay.

look.zh: 中央那根路灯柱把画面精确切成两半。
look.en: The central lamp post divides the canvas in exact halves.

src.file: File:Gustave Caillebotte - Paris Street; Rainy Day - Google Art Project.jpg

artist.zh: 皮埃尔-奥古斯特·雷诺阿

note.zh:
塞纳河畔沙图的富尔奈斯饭店露台。画中十四人全是雷诺阿的真实朋友：左下角逗小狗的是他未来的妻子阿丽娜，右侧反坐椅子的是画家卡耶博特，戴礼帽的是收藏家与业余史学家。

这是印象派最后的欢宴。雷诺阿此后转向更古典的画法，印象派团体也很快分裂。所有人物、酒瓶、葡萄、遮阳篷都沐浴在同一种被布篷过滤的柔光里——他花了几个月，让一场午餐看上去像即兴。
note.en:
The terrace of the Maison Fournaise at Chatou on the Seine. All fourteen figures are Renoir's actual friends: Aline, his future wife, plays with the dog at lower left; the painter Caillebotte sits backwards on a chair at the right; a collector-historian wears the top hat.

This is Impressionism's last party. Renoir soon turned toward a more classical manner and the group fractured. Every figure, bottle, grape and awning shares one soft light filtered through canvas — he worked for months to make a lunch look improvised.

look.zh: 每个人都是雷诺阿的真朋友，包括左下角那位未来的妻子。
look.en: Every face is a real friend of Renoir's, including his future wife at lower left.

src.file: File:Pierre-Auguste Renoir - Luncheon of the Boating Party - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
马奈的最后一幅大画，作于他去世前一年，当时他已行动困难，靠助手把模特与吧台搬进工作室。

镜子是全画的谜题：按物理，女招待的背影不该出现在右侧那么远的位置，那个与她交谈的男人也不该被她本人挡住。马奈故意让镜像「错位」，于是我们同时看到她的正面（孤独、疲惫、不在场）与她的社会角色（正在应对一位顾客）。吧台上的酒瓶与玻璃碗里的橘子，是他画过最好的静物。
note.en:
Manet's last large painting, made a year before his death when he could barely walk and had the bar and models carried into his studio.

The mirror is the puzzle: physically, the barmaid's reflected back should not sit that far to the right, and the man talking to her should not be hidden by her own body. Manet displaced the reflection deliberately, so we see at once her face — tired, absent, alone — and her social function, attending to a customer. The bottles and the bowl of oranges are the finest still life he ever painted.

look.zh: 镜中的倒影位置在物理上不成立——马奈故意错开了。
look.en: The reflection is physically impossible. Manet dislocated it on purpose.

src.file: File:Edouard Manet, A Bar at the Folies-Bergère.jpg

note.zh:
勃克林画了五个版本。一位刚丧夫的年轻寡妇委托他画一幅「可以用来做梦的画」，他把已完成的构图加上棺木与白衣人影，交给了她。

一叶小舟驶向被崖壁围抱的岛，中间是一片黑色柏树林。没有风、没有声音。这幅画在十九世纪末的德语世界几乎家家有复制品，纳博科夫说「柏林每一家都挂着」。拉赫玛尼诺夫为它写了一首交响诗，弗洛伊德、列宁、希特勒都收藏过复制品。
note.en:
Böcklin painted five versions. A young widow commissioned "a picture to dream by," and he added a coffin and a white-robed figure to a composition already under way and sent it to her.

A small boat approaches an island walled by cliffs, a grove of black cypresses at its centre. There is no wind and no sound. By 1900 reproductions hung in German homes everywhere — Nabokov said in every Berlin household. Rachmaninoff wrote a symphonic poem about it; Freud, Lenin and Hitler all owned copies.

look.zh: 没有风，水面完全静止——声音被从这幅画里删掉了。
look.en: No wind, no ripple. Sound has been deleted from this picture.

src.file: File:Arnold Böcklin - Die Toteninsel III (Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin).jpg

note.zh:
1884年沙龙上的丑闻。画中人是巴黎社交名媛维吉妮·高特罗。原作中她右肩的吊带是滑落的，观众哗然，她母亲要求撤画，萨金特拒绝，事后偷偷把吊带改回了肩上。

真正冒犯人的可能不是吊带，而是姿态：她扭身、抬下巴、把脸完全转开，皮肤被画成一种近乎尸体的珍珠白（她确实用含砷的粉底）。事件毁了萨金特在巴黎的生意，他移居伦敦。多年后他说：「这是我画过最好的一张。」
note.en:
The scandal of the 1884 Salon. The sitter is Virginie Gautreau, a Paris society figure. In the original the right shoulder strap had slipped off; the room was appalled, her mother demanded the picture be withdrawn, Sargent refused — and later quietly repainted the strap back onto the shoulder.

The real offence may not have been the strap but the pose: the torso twists, the chin lifts, the face turns fully away, and the skin is a pearl-white close to a corpse's (she did use arsenic-based powder). The affair destroyed his Paris practice and he moved to London. Years later he said it was the best thing he had ever done.

look.zh: 她右肩的吊带原本是滑落的——萨金特事后偷偷改了回去。
look.en: That right strap originally hung off the shoulder. Sargent quietly repainted it.

src.file: File:Madame X (Madame Pierre Gautreau), John Singer Sargent, 1884 (unfree frame crop).jpg

title.en: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte

note.zh:
修拉花了两年、画了六十多幅习作才完成这张。他不调色——所有颜色以纯色小点并置，由观者的眼睛在视网膜上完成混合，这就是「点彩」或他自称的「分色主义」。

但这不是一张轻松的野餐画。四十八个人物几乎都是侧面或背面，彼此不交谈，像埃及浮雕一样凝固。修拉画的是1880年代巴黎新兴中产阶级的周末：他们并肩坐着，却各自沉默。画框上的点彩边框也是他亲手所画。
note.en:
Seurat spent two years and more than sixty studies on this canvas. He refused to mix pigment: pure colours are set side by side as dots and combined by the viewer's eye, a method he called divisionism.

It is not a relaxed afternoon. Almost all forty-eight figures are shown in strict profile or from behind, none of them speaking, frozen like an Egyptian relief. What Seurat painted was the new Parisian middle class at leisure in the 1880s: sitting together and entirely separate. The pointillist border on the frame is his own work too.

look.zh: 退开五步再看——色点会自己混合成阳光。
look.en: Step back five paces. The dots mix themselves into sunlight.

src.file: File:A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, Georges Seurat, 1884.jpg

note.zh:
萨金特为了捕捉黄昏那几分钟的光，连续两个夏天每天只画二十分钟——太阳一落到特定角度就开工，光一变就停笔。冬天他把花园的花全部记录下来，第二年重新种回原位。

标题取自一首当时流行歌曲的歌词。灯笼的暖光与暮色的冷蓝在此刻恰好势均力敌，这是一天中唯一能同时看清两种光的时刻。这幅画让二十九岁的萨金特在伦敦重新立足——此前《X夫人》的丑闻几乎毁掉了他的巴黎事业。
note.en:
To catch the few minutes of dusk light, Sargent painted for about twenty minutes a day across two consecutive summers, starting when the sun reached a particular angle and stopping when it moved. Over winter he recorded the garden's planting and replaced it the following year.

The title comes from a popular song of the day. Lantern warmth and the cold blue of evening are exactly matched here — the one moment when both kinds of light can be seen at once. The picture re-established Sargent in London at twenty-nine, after the scandal of Madame X had all but destroyed his Paris practice.

look.zh: 每天只画二十分钟，画了两个夏天。
look.en: Twenty minutes a day, across two summers.

src.file: File:John Singer Sargent - Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
取自丁尼生的同名诗：受诅咒的女子只能透过镜子看世界，一旦直视兰斯洛特，诅咒降临。她解开小舟的缆绳，唱着歌漂向卡美洛，途中死去。

沃特豪斯选的是她刚放开锁链的那一刻。船头三支蜡烛已灭两支；船身铺着她织了一生的挂毯，上面正是她从镜中看到的那些景象。她张着嘴——那首歌还没唱完。整幅画的悲剧感来自一个细节：她终于看见了真实的世界，代价是只能看这一次。
note.en:
From Tennyson's poem: a cursed woman may see the world only through a mirror, and the moment she looks directly at Lancelot the curse falls. She unties a boat, sings as she drifts toward Camelot, and dies on the way.

Waterhouse chose the instant she releases the chain. Two of the three candles at the prow have gone out. Draped over the hull is the tapestry she spent her life weaving — the very scenes she had watched in the mirror. Her mouth is open; the song is not finished. The tragedy is in one fact: she finally sees the real world, and may only see it once.

look.zh: 船头三支蜡烛，已经灭了两支。
look.en: Three candles at the prow. Two are already out.

src.file: File:John William Waterhouse - The Lady of Shalott - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
梵高在阿尔勒画向日葵，是为了装饰高更即将入住的房间。他给提奥写信说要画「一整套向日葵的交响曲」，最后完成了七幅，这是其中最著名的一幅。

他几乎只用黄色作画——背景黄、桌面黄、花瓶黄、花黄——却让每一种黄都不同。这是极难的技术挑战：没有对比色帮忙，全靠冷暖与厚薄拉开层次。花朵从盛开到枯萎全在同一只瓶里，是一幅关于时间的静物。
note.en:
Van Gogh painted sunflowers in Arles to decorate the room Gauguin was coming to occupy. He wrote to Theo of a "symphony in blue and yellow" and finished seven canvases; this is the best known.

He worked almost entirely in yellow — yellow ground, yellow table, yellow vase, yellow flowers — and made every yellow different. It is a brutal technical problem: with no complementary to help, the separation has to come from warmth and thickness alone. The blooms range from full flower to seed head in one jar: a still life about time.

look.zh: 一整幅画只用黄色拉开层次——没有对比色帮忙。
look.en: The whole picture separates in yellow alone, with no complementary to help.

src.file: File:Vincent Willem van Gogh 127.jpg

note.zh:
梵高说这幅画要表达「绝对的休息」，颜色的简化是刻意的：「阴影和投影都被取消了，用平涂的鲜明色块，像日本版画那样。」

墙面原本是紫色（颜料褪色后成了今天的蓝），地板是破碎的红。透视被扭曲：右墙倾斜，床与地板的角度对不上——他不是画错了，房间本身就是梯形的。所有物件成双：两把椅子、两幅肖像、两只枕头。而他独居于此。
note.en:
Van Gogh said the picture had to express "absolute rest," and the simplification is deliberate: "shadows and cast shadows are suppressed; it is coloured in flat, frank tints like Japanese prints."

The walls were originally violet — pigment fading has left today's blue — and the floor a broken red. Perspective is skewed: the right wall leans, bed and floorboards do not agree. He was not making mistakes; the room really was trapezoidal. Everything comes in pairs: two chairs, two portraits, two pillows. He lived there alone.

look.zh: 所有东西都成双：两把椅子、两只枕头、两幅画。他一个人住。
look.en: Everything is doubled — two chairs, two pillows, two portraits. He lived alone.

src.file: File:Vincent van Gogh - De slaapkamer - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
梵高第一幅带星空的画，比《星月夜》早一年。他在信里得意地说：这幅画里「没有用一点黑色」——夜晚是用深蓝、紫和绿画成的。

他真的把画架搬到阿尔勒的福鲁姆广场上，夜里在煤气灯下作画。天文学家用星图核对过：画中的星象与1888年9月16日晚阿尔勒的夜空吻合。那家咖啡馆今天还在，被漆成了画里的黄色。
note.en:
Van Gogh's first painting with a starry sky, a year before The Starry Night. He wrote with satisfaction that it contains "no black at all" — the night is made of deep blue, violet and green.

He did set his easel up on the Place du Forum in Arles and worked at night under the gas lamps. Astronomers have matched the star positions to the sky over Arles on 16 September 1888. The café still stands, now painted the yellow of the picture.

look.zh: 整幅夜景没有用一点黑色。
look.en: There is no black anywhere in this night.

src.file: File:Vincent Willem van Gogh - Cafe Terrace at Night (Yorck).jpg

note.zh:
布列塔尼的农妇听完布道，眼前浮现雅各与天使摔跤的景象。高更把地面涂成纯粹的朱红——不是写实，而是「幻象的颜色」。这一步在1888年是革命性的：颜色第一次脱离了它所描绘的对象。

一棵斜插的苹果树把画面分成两半：左下是现实中低头祈祷的白帽农妇，右上是她们心里看见的东西。构图直接学自浮世绘。高更把这幅画送给当地教堂，被神父拒收。
note.en:
Breton women, coming out of a sermon, see Jacob wrestling the angel. Gauguin painted the ground pure vermilion — not observed, but the colour of a vision. In 1888 that was revolutionary: colour cut loose from the thing it describes.

A diagonal apple tree splits the canvas: below left, the real women in white coifs with their heads bowed; above right, what they see. The composition is borrowed straight from Japanese prints. Gauguin offered the painting to the local church, and the priest refused it.

look.zh: 地面是纯朱红——这是幻象的颜色，不是草地的颜色。
look.en: The ground is pure vermilion: the colour of the vision, not of grass.

src.file: File:La vision après le sermon (Paul Gauguin).jpg

note.zh:
这是梵高在圣雷米精神疗养院里，凭记忆与想象画下的凌晨天空。他在给弟弟提奥的信里说，自己「需要夜晚来画星星」。天上十一颗星、一弯残月，全部被卷成漩涡；而山下的村庄安静、笔触平直，两种笔法的对撞就是这幅画的全部张力。

左侧那株柏树像一簇黑色火焰直插天空——在南法，柏树种在墓园边，是死亡的树。梵高把它画成连接大地与星辰的通道，这是他一生中最接近宗教感的一张画。
note.en:
Painted from memory in the asylum at Saint-Rémy, this is the sky before dawn as Van Gogh reconstructed it. He told his brother Theo he "needed the night in order to paint the stars." Eleven stars and a waning moon are churned into spirals, while the village below is rendered in short, level strokes — the collision of the two handwritings is the whole drama of the picture.

The cypress on the left rises like black flame. In Provence cypresses are planted at cemeteries; Van Gogh turned the tree of death into the one thing joining earth to the stars.

look.zh: 注意村庄的笔触是平的，只有天空在旋转——动静全在笔法里。
look.en: The village is painted in flat strokes; only the sky turns. All the motion is in the brushwork.

src.file: File:Van Gogh - Starry Night - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
1888年圣诞前夜与高更激烈争执后，梵高割下自己左耳的一部分。这幅画作于事发后约三周，他刚出院回到黄房子。

绷带在右耳——因为他对着镜子作画。背后墙上挂着一幅日本浮世绘（歌川派的富士山图），画架空着。他望向侧前方，眼神平静得有些反常。三个月后他自愿进入圣雷米疗养院。
note.en:
After a violent quarrel with Gauguin on Christmas Eve 1888, Van Gogh cut off part of his left ear. This was painted about three weeks later, just after he came home from hospital to the Yellow House.

The bandage appears on the right because he worked from a mirror. A Japanese print hangs behind him and the easel is empty. He looks slightly off to one side, with a calm that is almost unsettling. Three months later he committed himself to the asylum at Saint-Rémy.

look.zh: 绷带在右耳，因为他对着镜子画——受伤的是左耳。
look.en: The bandage is on the right because he worked from a mirror. The wound was on the left.

src.file: File:Vincent van Gogh - Self-portrait with bandaged ear (1889, Courtauld Institute).jpg

note.zh:
常被当作梵高的绝笔（其实不是，但确实作于他去世前几周）。他在信里描述这批双宽幅画布：「广阔的麦田在乱云之下，我不必刻意表达悲伤与极度孤独。」

三条路从前景分岔，其中一条通向画外，另外两条消失在麦浪里，都没有终点。乌鸦从远处朝我们飞来，越靠近越大。构图有意让人无处落脚——这是绘画里少见的、结构本身就令人不安的作品。
note.en:
Often called Van Gogh's last painting. It is not, though it comes from his final weeks. He described these double-square canvases to his brother: "vast fields of wheat under troubled skies, and I did not need to go out of my way to express sadness and extreme loneliness."

Three paths fork out of the foreground; one leaves the picture, two dissolve in the wheat, none arrives. The crows fly toward us, growing larger as they come. The composition deliberately offers nowhere to stand — rare in painting, a structure that is itself distressing.

look.zh: 三条路都没有终点，乌鸦正朝你飞来。
look.en: None of the three paths arrives anywhere, and the crows are flying at you.

src.file: File:Vincent van Gogh - Wheatfield with crows - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
1890年1月，弟弟提奥来信说儿子出生，取名文森特。梵高立刻开始画这张——杏树是普罗旺斯最早开花的树，是新生的标志。他把它送给弟弟一家挂在床头。

构图完全来自日本版画：没有地平线，枝条从画面各边切入，天空是一整片不变的蓝。这也是他画得最平静的一幅，几乎没有那种焦虑的旋涡笔触。五个月后他去世；提奥半年后也随之而去。
note.en:
In January 1890 Theo wrote that his son had been born and named Vincent. Van Gogh started this at once — almond is the first tree to flower in Provence, the sign of new life — and sent it for the couple to hang above their bed.

The composition is purely Japanese: no horizon, branches entering from every edge, sky an unbroken sheet of blue. It is also the calmest thing he painted, almost free of the anxious spiralling stroke. He died five months later; Theo followed within six months.

look.zh: 这是送给刚出生的侄子的礼物——也是他最平静的一张画。
look.en: A gift for his newborn nephew, and the calmest picture he ever made.

src.file: File:Vincent van Gogh - Almond blossom - Google Art Project.jpg

note.zh:
作于梵高生命的最后两个月。他写信给妹妹说，这张画里建筑「几乎是紫色的，衬着纯净的深蓝天空」，而这种蓝「比我在纽南画的老教堂更有表现力」。

教堂没有一扇窗透出光，全部是黑洞。地面的小路在门前分成两条，绕过教堂两侧——没有一条通向门口。他曾想当牧师，被教会拒绝。这幅画里的建筑在扭动，只有地上的阳光是安稳的。
note.en:
Painted in Van Gogh's last two months. He wrote to his sister that the building here is "almost violet against a sky of pure deep blue," and that this blue was more expressive than the old church he had painted at Nuenen.

Not one window admits light; they are all black holes. The path divides in front of the church and runs around both sides — neither branch reaches the door. He had once wanted to be a pastor and was turned down. The architecture writhes; only the sunlight on the ground is steady.

look.zh: 小路在门前分开、绕过两侧——没有一条通往门口。
look.en: The path splits and passes on both sides. Neither branch reaches the door.
